--- title: "Chapter 6: Simple Linear Regression" subtitle: "STAT117: Introduction to Statistics" format: revealjs: width: 1050 height: 1050 margin: 0 theme: default slide-number: true transition: fade toc: false self-contained: false smaller: false scrollable: true chalkboard: buttons: true template-partials: - title-slide.html editor_options: chunk_output_type: inline --- ## Setup You want to *predict* something (e.g., predict stock prices; predict a person's marathon finish time; predict a student's social economic status `SES`) > In reality, the main goal can be the prediction itself, or can be understanding what variables are important for making the prediction. I) The “something” you are predicting: II) The variable(s) you would use to make a prediction: - For instance, what variables would you use to predict a student `SES`?



We'll only cover these two cases: - Case 1: Y is scale and X is scale (called `Covariate`) - Case 2: Y is scale and X is dichotomous (called `Factor`) ## Example Label the dependent (Y) and independent (X) variables: 1. Use a student's SAT score to predict the student's GPA in college
2. Predict a student's satisfaction with Drew's dining service by whether the student is an international student
3. Predict your future salary based on your GPA in college
4. Use `achmat08` to predict `achrdg08`
> Jamovi procedure: Analyze – Regression – Linear Regression; Numeric predictors go in the `Covariates` box, and categorical predictors go in the `Factors` box. # Case 1: Numeric predictor ## SES and achmat08 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="R code (optional)"} nels <- haven::read_sav("../../../../dataset/NELS.sav") plot( nels$achmat08, nels$ses, xlab = "Math achievement in 8th grade (achmat08)", ylab = "SES", pch = 16 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](chapter_6_slide_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot of eighth-grade math achievement and socioeconomic status, with a fitted regression line' width=120%} ::: ::: As a review, is there a relationship between `achmat08` and `SES`? (Pearson r = 0.318)

Can you provide an estimate of SES, if a student's `achmat08` score is - around 45? - around 70? ## Regression line The goal is to find the line that “best fits” the data. The (least squares) regression line minimizes the total “distance” of each point to the line, where distance is measured by the squared difference. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="R code (optional)"} nels <- haven::read_sav("../../../../dataset/NELS.sav") plot( nels$achmat08, nels$ses, xlab = "Math achievement in 8th grade (achmat08)", ylab = "SES", pch = 16 ) abline(lm(ses ~ achmat08, data = nels), col = "#D36B43", lwd = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](chapter_6_slide_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot of eighth-grade math achievement and socioeconomic status, with a fitted regression line' width=120%} ::: ::: ## Jamovi output **Model Fit Measures** | Model | R | R$^2$ | |---:|---:|---:| | 1 | 0.318 | 0.101 | **Model Coefficients - ses** | Predictor | Estimate | SE | t | p | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | Intercept | 5.082 | 1.8064 | 2.81 | .005 | | achmat08 | 0.236 | 0.0315 | 7.49 | <.001 | Recall, the form of a line is given by:

> HAT notation is very important! ## Predictions $\hat{Y} = 5.082 + 0.236 \cdot X$ $\hat{SES} = 5.082 + 0.236 \cdot achmat08$ - What is the predicted SES for a student with an `achmat08` score of 45?
Be cautious about predicting out of the range of X - What is the predicted SES for a student with an `achmat08` score of 10? ## Residuals $\hat{SES} = 5.082 + 0.236 \cdot achmat08$ Selected students from the NELS dataset: | Student ID | `achmat08` | `ses` | |---:|---:|---:| | 374 | 44.80 | 21 | | 489 | 44.80 | 20 | | 67 | 70.04 | 27 | | 207 | 69.93 | 11 | - Residual = actual - predicted = `ses` - $\hat{SES}$ What is the residual for student with ID 374? ## Interpretations $\hat{SES} = 5.082 + 0.236 \cdot achmat08$ - Slope


- Intercept


## Regression and scatterplot ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="R code (optional)"} nels <- haven::read_sav("../../../../dataset/NELS.sav") plot( nels$achmat08, nels$ses, xlab = "Math achievement in 8th grade (achmat08)", ylab = "SES", pch = 16 ) abline(lm(ses ~ achmat08, data = nels), col = "#D36B43", lwd = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](chapter_6_slide_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot of eighth-grade math achievement and socioeconomic status, with a fitted regression line' width=120%} ::: ::: ## Example: Icecream (Icecream.sav) We want to use temperature to predict the number of ice cream bars sold. a) Write down the regression line.

b) Provide the value of the intercept and give an interpretation.

c) Provide the value of the slope and give an interpretation.

d) For a day with a temperature of ____ Fahrenheit, how many ice cream bars do you estimate to be sold?

e) For day ID=12, are we over-predicting or under-predicting? Calculate the residual. # Case 2: dichotomous predictor ## SES and nursery school (yes/no) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="R code (optional)"} nels <- haven::read_sav("../../../../dataset/NELS.sav") plot( nels$nursery, nels$ses, xlab = "Nursery school attendance (nursery)", ylab = "SES", pch = 16 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](chapter_6_slide_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){fig-alt='Scatterplot of nursery school attendance and socioeconomic status, with a fitted regression line' width=120%} ::: ::: Can you estimate a student's SES if the student... - has not attend nursery school? - has attended nursery school? ## General idea Predict `SES` based on `Nursery`: essentially, this means we predict `SES` for the two values of `Nursery`: - If `Nursery` = Yes, we predict `SES` to be ________ - If `Nursery` = No, we predict `SES` to be ________
Show descriptives (Analyses -> Exploration -> Descriptives) **Descriptives** | Statistic | `nursery` | `ses` | |---|---|---:| | N | No | 139 | | | Yes | 281 | | Mean | No | 15.1 | | | Yes | 20.7 | | Median | No | 16.0 | | | Yes | 21.0 |
We can get the same results from a regression analysis! ## Example: Nursery Use regression to predict `SES` using `Nursery` (coded as 0=No, 1=Yes). > Make sure to put `Nursery` as a **factor**! (For dichotomous predictors, you can get the same correct coefficients if you put it as a covariate, but this is not recommended, as you will get incorrect information when the variable is nominal or ordinal, or is coded in a non-standard way.) a) Write down the regression line.

b) For a student who did attend nursery, what is the estimated SES?

c) For a student who did not attend nursery, what is the estimated SES?

d) Provide the value of the intercept and give an interpretation.

e) Provide the value of the slope and give an interpretation.

f) For student with ID=1, what is the residual? Are we over-predicting or under-predicting? ## Example: Computer Use regression to predict `SES` by whether or not the family owned a `computer` (coded as 0=No, 1=Yes). a) Write down the regression line.

b) For a student whose family had a computer, what is the estimated `SES`?

c) For a student whose family did not have a computer, what is the estimated `SES`?

d) Provide the value of the intercept and give an interpretation.

e) Provide the value of the slope and give an interpretation.

f) For student with ID=1, what is the residual? Are we over-predicting or under-predicting? ## Example: slope interpretation The following table is adapted from a 2020 publication, [*Training for a (half‐)marathon: Training volume and longest endurance run related to performance and running injuries*](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7496388/). For each predictor, interpret the number given in the "Estimate" column. Significant predictors of marathon finish time (in min): | Predictor | Estimate | |---|---:| | Sex (female) | 10.78 | | BMI (kg/m²) | 1.58 | | Running experience (years) | -0.42 | | Longest endurance run (km): <25 | 13.44 |

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
